key_insight: The paper develops a dynamic k-ω RANS closure for coarse-grained turbulence simulation that adapts its model coefficient from the flow itself, improving robustness under temporal coarsening.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more reliable and flexible turbulence model for engineering CFD where reduced temporal resolution is needed, while still capturing transition and boundary-layer separation/reattachment effects.
method: Build on temporally filtered Navier-Stokes equations as a unifying coarse-grained turbulence framework.
Derive a dynamic RANS closure based on the k-ω model, including an alternative form that avoids non-physical free-stream turbulence decay.
Validate through scale-resolving simulations and compare behavior under different temporal coarsening levels and free-stream turbulence settings.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a simulation campaign showing the new dynamic k-ω model remains robust to temporal coarsening and captures laminar-to-turbulent transition plus separation/reattachment sensitivity to inlet free-stream turbulence.
watch_item: Performance depends on the chosen free-stream turbulence prescription and the model’s behavior should be checked carefully in highly separated or boundary-condition-sensitive flows.
paper_title: Development of a class of dynamic RANS closures for coarse-grained approaches to turbulence
